observation.visible_scene: An abandoned concrete stairwell with a doorway showing bare winter trees behind it. In the foreground a metal table frame wrapped in yellow-and-black hazard tape supports a flat pane of greenish tempered glass that is already fully crazed/shattered. A black kettlebell rests upright near the center of the glass. The camera is essentially fixed on this setup for the whole excerpt.
visible_changes: The center of the glass pane progressively bows/sags downward under the kettlebell: at t=0 the pane is nearly flat with only a slight dip, while by the last frame the middle has bent into a deep V that hangs visibly below the level of the hazard-taped table edge.

The white crushed/shattered zone directly beneath the kettlebell enlarges as the sag increases, and the kettlebell settles a little lower relative to the table edge while keeping roughly the same horizontal position and upright handle orientation.

A stream of glass fragments and dust falls from beneath the sagging pane. It begins as a small puff in the early frames and grows into a continuous, widening cascade of shards by the middle and end of the excerpt.
The background (stairs, doorway, trees) and the table/tape frame remain in place, indicating the motion is deformation of the glass and falling debris, not scene translation.
outside_clip_unknowns: The impact or drop that originally cracked the glass is not shown; the pane is already shattered at the first frame.
Whether the glass ultimately fails completely and the kettlebell falls through, or the debris stream stops, is not visible within the crop.
The cause of the continuing fragmentation (load creep, vibration, crack propagation) cannot be determined from the frames alone.
uncertain_details: Any slight camera drift or zoom is minimal and not clearly supported; treated as near-static.
Exact material identity of the glass and the kettlebell mass are inferred only from appearance.
Small shifts of the kettlebell handle tilt between frames are within measurement uncertainty and may be settling rather than distinct motion.
